narrative.overview:
AtlasScope is the brand. Agent Kit is its first product, and atlasscope.dev is the Agent Kit site. The system is the AtlasScope identity applied to a working tool: a near-black ink ground, white type, one raised slate tone, one muted grey, and nothing else. The name "Monolithic Minimal" is the owner's own reference board (black and white, a lit planet horizon, white pill buttons); it is used here as the working name for the system.

The homepage carries the one image the system allows, a photograph of a planet horizon, sitting under a solid ink header and above a solid ink strip that holds the install command. Everything a visitor acts on (the command and the Copy button) sits on a solid ground, never on the photograph.

The rest of the site is a library, a first-app guide, a few reading pages and an account area. These follow the visitor's light or dark setting. Dark is the brand set. Light is the same system turned over: cool grey paper, white raised panels, ink type and ink buttons. Both sets are neutral and cool, with no warm tint.

The system has no accent hue. Emphasis comes from contrast, from weight, and from the typeface: anything a visitor can type or paste is set in Geist Mono, and that is what marks it as a command.
keyCharacteristics: Four colours on dark surfaces: ink, white, slate, muted. Rules are muted mixed over ink.
A cool light set for library pages: paper #F4F5F7, white panels, ink type, grey rules.
The header and the homepage are ink in both the light and the dark setting.
Montserrat 600 for display, Geist for text, Geist Mono for commands.
One primary action per view. In the hero it is a white pill; on library pages it is a solid ink (or, in dark, white) button.
One photograph, used only as the homepage hero backdrop under a solid header.
The AtlasScope logo is ink or white only, sits on a solid field, and is never scaled.

rules.name: The Four Colours Rule
rules.body: Dark surfaces use ink, white, slate and muted, and nothing else. The two rule colours are muted mixed over ink, not new colours.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: The light set is neutral and cool. Paper, raised white and sunk grey make the surfaces; ink and two greys make the type. No warm paper, no amber.

rules.name: The No Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no accent hue. A command is marked by Geist Mono, a primary action by the solid button, a selection by contrast and an underline.

rules.name: The Ink Everywhere Rule
rules.body: The header and the homepage are ink in both the light and the dark setting. They do not follow the visitor's light preference.

rules.name: The Dots Only Rule
rules.body: The six section hues appear only as small dots. They are not fills, borders, text colours, card tints or button tints.

rules.name: The Danger Only Rule
rules.body: The danger colour marks destruction and errors and nothing else.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is a 2px outline in the focus colour (white on dark, ink on light), 2px off the element.

rules.name: The Three Faces Rule
rules.body: Montserrat 600 for display, Geist for text, Geist Mono for commands. The wordmark is drawn as outlines; never retype it in live Montserrat.

rules.name: The No Label Above Rule
rules.body: No small label sits above a heading. A headline is the first thing in its block. On detail pages the kicker (kind, group, version, id) sits under the title and lead.

rules.name: The One H1 Rule
rules.body: Each page has one h1. Headings inside imported skill text are shifted down a level so they never compete with it.

rules.name: The Read Before Paste Rule
rules.body: A command is never cut off on a phone. Below 720px it wraps and shows in full, so it can be read before it is pasted.

rules.name: The Solid Ground Rule
rules.body: Anything a visitor operates or needs to read exactly (the header, the logo, the install command) sits on a solid colour, never on the photograph.

rules.name: The One Movement Rule
rules.body: The only animation that plays by itself on the homepage is the photograph settling into place on load (1400ms, from 55% opacity and 3.5% oversize). Text is in place from the first frame. With reduced motion set, nothing moves.

rules.name: The One Primary Rule
rules.body: One primary action per view: a white pill in the hero, a solid button on library pages. A second action beside it is outlined. Two primaries never sit side by side.

rules.name: The Untouched Logo Rule
rules.body: The header logo is pixel-fitted. Never scale it, transform it, or set its size from CSS. The logo is ink or white only: no gradient, glow, outline or tint.

rules.name: The One Photograph Rule
rules.body: The orbit photograph is the only image in the system. It is used as supplied, only as the homepage hero backdrop, and only under a solid header.

dos: Do build dark surfaces from ink (#0B0C12), white, slate (#151821) and muted (#A3A6AD) only, with hairlines at #2C2E34 and control borders at #66686F.
Do build light surfaces from paper (#F4F5F7), white, sunk grey (#E8EAEE), ink and the two text greys (#2B2F3A, #5A5F6B), with hairlines at #DCDFE5 and control borders at #808693.
Do keep the header and the homepage ink in both the light and the dark setting.
Do set the header as the AtlasScope lockup, a 1px divider, then "Agent Kit", in that order.
Do set every command and id in Geist Mono; that is what marks it.
Do use one primary action per view and an outlined button for the second.
Do put the install command and the logo on a solid colour.
Do offset sticky columns and jump targets by `--header-h`.
Do show a full command on phones, wrapped, so it can be read before it is pasted.
Do name Copy buttons by what they copy, and show a plain message next to a form when it fails.
Do read counts from generated content.
donts: Don't add an accent hue, or use amber or warm paper anywhere.
Don't use a section hue as a fill, border, text colour or card tint; the six hues are small dots.
Don't use the danger colour for anything but destruction and errors.
Don't give a callout a coloured side border.
Don't place the AtlasScope logo on the photograph or on any image.
Don't scale, transform, recolour, outline or shade the header logo, and don't retype the wordmark in live text.
Don't put a small label above a heading.
Don't add a second image, crop or regrade the orbit photograph for effect, or use it anywhere but the homepage hero.
Don't put two primary buttons in one view.
Don't animate text into place; only the photograph moves, once, on load.
